executive_summary: This collection window (November 17 - 23, 2026) is the seventh full week after fashion month's close and the twenty-second archived window overall. The CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund's 2026 winner, scheduled for an October 20 gala, was re-checked with fresh search; as of search time, still no dated, sourced coverage naming an actual winner has surfaced from CFDA, Vogue, WWD, Business of Fashion, or Fashionista -- available coverage remains limited to the June finalist announcement and the October 20 gala date. This is now the fifth consecutive window (2026-10-26, 2026-11-02, 2026-11-09, 2026-11-16, 2026-11-23) in which the signal remains open, roughly five weeks past the gala with zero indexed post-event coverage of an outcome. Separately, the CFDA Fashion Awards (distinct from the Fashion Fund) remains unconfirmed for 2026 -- fresh search this window, including a targeted postponed/canceled query, again found no date, nominee list, or post-event coverage, now the fourth consecutive window this question has been open, with no evidence of postponement or cancellation either. This window also checked broader in-window discourse specifically for Thanksgiving/Black Friday retail signal, since that is a genuine, recurring US fashion-calendar event falling within this window's dates (Black Friday itself lands November 27, 2026, just after this window closes). Search found dated, named-retailer confirmation that early Black Friday/holiday sale windows are already running during Nov 17-23 (e.g. JCPenney's early-access sale beginning Nov 9, Target's main event beginning Nov 22, Macy's doorbuster window beginning Nov 22), which is logged as a genuine retail-calendar signal distinct from garment/aesthetic trend discourse -- it is commerce-calendar timing, not a style signal, and is classified and caveated as such. No other in-window garment, silhouette, or aesthetic discourse independently verifiable to this window was found; general forecast content encountered in search (color-of-2026 picks, quarter-zip/polo-knit forecasts, occasionwear roundups) was dated to earlier 2026 publications, not in-window reporting, and is excluded from this report's signals accordingly. On balance this window's honest read remains thin, continuing the post-fashion-month quiet stretch, with both institutional questions still open and one new, narrowly-scoped retail-calendar signal added.

top_signals.human_editor_note: Five consecutive windows with zero indexed coverage of a CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund winner is well outside ordinary reporting lag for a program this well-covered in prior years. This report does not speculate a winner's identity, does not assume the gala was cancelled or the result withheld, and does not backfill from memory or analogy to other Fashion Fund programs. The most defensible reading remains either (a) a search-tool recency/indexing gap specific to this query that has now persisted across five windows, or (b) a genuine change in how this cycle's outcome was publicized. Both remain stated as open possibilities, not conclusions. If dated coverage appears in a future window, reconcile and close this signal_id there with a real name and source; do not edit this or prior reports retroactively without new evidence.

top_signals.name: Early Black Friday / holiday retail sale windows already running (Nov 17-23) ahead of Nov 27 Black Friday

Multiple named retailers have publicly dated early-access/holiday sale windows overlapping Nov 17-23: JCPenney's early-access sale beginning Nov 9, Target's early deals beginning Nov 6 with its main Black Friday event beginning Nov 22, and Macy's doorbuster window beginning Nov 22. This is retailer-published calendar timing, corroborated by retail-calendar aggregator coverage (e.g. Calculatorian, MyWeeklyAds, Alibaba product-insights), not editorial trend reporting.
top_signals.index_note: New this window. Logged as a retail-calendar/commerce-timing signal, distinct in kind from a garment/aesthetic/silhouette trend -- it describes when discounting starts, not what is being worn or designed. Included because the task explicitly asked whether the Thanksgiving/Black Friday retail calendar produces any real in-window signal; it does, but only at this commerce-calendar level, not as style discourse.
top_signals.human_editor_note: This signal is intentionally narrow: it confirms that early Black Friday promotional windows are dated and running during Nov 17-23, 2026, per named retailers' own published schedules. It does not assert anything about apparel trend content, sales volume outcomes, or consumer behavior -- those would require post-event reporting not yet available inside this window. Retail-calendar aggregator sites are the corroborating sources rather than primary editorial outlets, so confidence is capped at medium despite multiple retailers being named.
